messages:
maria: quick thought after the RFC review: we need explicit semantics for 'advisory' vs 'gate' plugin outcomes and how humans see them in Console.
dan: agreed. my take: advisory = metadata + trends, gate = prevents registry promotion. both should be surfaced, but gates trigger an automated 'require-review' workflow.
lee: important to include TTLs for advisory signals. if a plugin flags a transient env mismatch (e.g., cuda driver minor), it shouldn't block forever. suggest advisory TTL + re-eval triggers.
sasha: +1 on TTLs. also propose an 'escalation policy' per-model: after N advisory hits in M days escalate to human. makes noisy checks actionable.
al: operational note  (ignore)
maria: al? you there?
al: oops pasted junk, sorry. re: storage, we should attach plugin artifacts (logs, perf traces, diffs) to registry entry and keep a compact summary for Console. full artifacts can live in S3 with signed refs.
dan: how do we handle costy microbench runs for every push? we should support 'delta runs' that only run heavy plugins when model binary changes beyond a fingerprint threshold. cheap checksum vs content-aware fingerprinting.
sasha: fingerprint rules: binary-hash + model-config-hash + tokenizer-hash. if none change, skip heavy runs. but also have forced-rebench flag for safety.
lee: sampling for golden tests: rotate input shards and keep seed metadata. important for reproducibility: store random seeds + exact container image + plugin version for every run.
maria: UI: show a timeline of plugin successes/fails with hover to expand artifacts and a single 'acceptance score' with breakdown. acceptance thresholds come from team policy files in repo.
dan: on rollouts: registry should allow pinning a model version to canary groups only if passes gate. allow a 'fast-fail' toggle to opt into stricter gating for critical customers.
sasha: security: plugins run in sandboxed containers with resource cgroups and a network egress policy. otherwise a malicious model could exfil via a plugin callback.
al: integration point: make plugin manifest a small JSON schema and store it alongside model metadata so older registries still know how to interpret results. plugin_id @ semver is mandatory.
maria: next steps: small spike to implement prototype aggregator + Console mock (dan), plugin runner sandbox (al), and storage/manifest prototype (sasha). target: 10d spike, then RFC v2.
dan: will sketch candidate scoring algorithm: base score 100, subtract weighted penalties, clamp [0,100], thresholds map to allow/review/block. share in PR.
lee: I'll prototype TTL & re-eval rules in the job-pool.
sasha: i'll draft plugin manifest schema and sandbox checklist.
eng-bot: tickets created: ONBOARD-801 (aggregator spike), ONBOARD-802 (sandbox runner), ONBOARD-803 (manifest + storage). assigned: dan, al, sasha.
maria: thanks team — let's capture these in the RFC follow-up doc and sync next Tues. :calendar:
